title: 4 HOURS AGO •Track News Get Your Tickets: Arlington On Sale Now, Long Beach Available Sunday Tickets for the Java House Grand Prix of Arlington (photo), which was a popular success with fans its inaugural year in 2026, are on sale now.
excerpt:
Single-day ticket options for the 2027 Java House Grand Prix of Arlington are on sale now at gparlington.com.

The Java House Grand Prix of Arlington (photo, top) returns Friday, March 19 through Sunday, March 21 to the streets of Arlington, Texas, following a record-breaking inaugural event that welcomed tens of thousands of fans to Arlington’s Entertainment District. The stars of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES are back in North Texas for a weekend of world-class racing and entertainment.

Three-day ticket packages, paddock passes and parking also remain available while supplies last.

The Java House Grand Prix of Arlington features a 2.73-mile temporary street circuit woven throughout Arlington's Entertainment District. The challenging, 14-turn course provides fans with a unique opportunity to experience the speed, sound and excitement of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES in one of the country's premier sports and entertainment destinations.

Fans can get even closer to the action with the purchase of a paddock pass, for exclusive garage access where INDYCAR teams work on their race cars all weekend long. The event also features a variety of premium viewing experiences, including reserved grandstand seating and the WinStar Winners Club.

The WinStar Winners Club delivers an unparalleled Race Day experience, featuring tiered seating, high-top tables and bar rails with exceptional views of pit lane, the front straightaway and Turn 1. A portion of the club extends directly over the racetrack, offering guests the thrilling perspective of “The Fastest Racing on Earth” directly beneath them.

Adding to the exclusivity, the winner's podium is integrated into the WinStar Winners Club, providing guests with an up-close view of the victory celebrations following every race throughout the weekend – an experience unique to the INDYCAR schedule. All-inclusive amenities include food, beer, wine, spirits, soft drinks, water, paddock access and parking.

Single day practice tickets start at $20, and Race Day tickets start at $100. Fans can get 3-day tickets starting at $150. Children under 12 are admitted free in general admission areas at the Java House Grand Prix of Arlington when accompanied by an adult general admission ticketholder.

Long Beach Tickets Go On Sale Sunday, Oct. 18

Tickets go on sale at 1 p.m. ET Sunday, Oct. 18 for the 2027 Acura Grand Prix of Long Beach, the longest-running street race on the NTT INDYCAR SERIES schedule. The annual festival of speed in Southern California (photo, above) takes place Friday, April 16 through Sunday, April 18 on the iconic 11-turn, 1.968-mile street circuit.

Starting at 1 p.m. ET Sunday, fans can select and pay for their 2027 Acura Grand Prix of Long Beach seats, parking and paddock passes online at gplb.com. Ticket orders can also be placed by calling the toll-free ticket hotline, (888) 827-7333.

Off the track and free to all race attendees will be the popular Lifestyle Expo featuring more than 100 exhibitors showcasing the latest in automotive, travel, home, sustainability, fitness and recreation as well as the large Family Fun Zone in the Long Beach Arena. There will also be Friday and Saturday evening concerts, more than 150 concession stands throughout the venue, unique car displays, driver autograph sessions, the CARnival car show and a wide variety of activities for everyone.

Ticket prices range from $59 for a Friday General Admission ticket to $232 for a three-day ticket that includes Saturday/Sunday reserved seating in grandstand upper levels. Prepaid parking packages are also available, along with ADA seating, NTT INDYCAR SERIES paddock passes, Super Photo tickets and a wide variety of hospitality packages. Children 12 years and under will be admitted free with a ticketed adult, although they will need a Junior ticket to sit in the grandstands.

title: 1 day ago •Driver News Alex Palou To Rev Up Indiana Football Fans Before Buckeye Showdown
excerpt:
1 day ago

Alex Palou has a new role for Saturday’s college football showdown between Indiana University and Ohio State on FOX. He’s the honorary driver of an Indiana University-themed NTT INDYCAR SERIES race car.

Palou was named Thursday to fill in for Hoosier the Bison, IU’s mascot, who has driven the car while leading the Hoosiers out of the tunnel before each home game at Memorial Stadium this season.

The five-time NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion, a native of Spain, has become an avid Indiana University sports fan since making Indianapolis his home. He also has visited IU’s Bloomington campus several times ahead of big games as part of FOX Sports’ promotional activities.

“I’m following IU now,” Palou said during FOX Sports’ “Big Noon Kickoff” before a game last year. “It’s (IU atmosphere) a little more rowdy than I thought. I love it.”

Palou’s honorary role is the latest stop in a busy stretch behind the wheel of a variety of race cars -- none of them his No. 10 Chip Ganassi Racing Honda.

On Oct. 3, he competed in the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship’s Petit Le Mans for Meyer Shank Racing. He then drove the No. 80 Lone Star Racing Mercedes-AMG in last weekend’s Intercontinental GT Challenge Indianapolis 8 Hour during practice and qualifying but never turned a wheel in the race due to being taken out in an accident before his first stint. On Monday, Palou tested the IR-28, the new NTT INDYCAR SERIES chassis scheduled to debut in 2028, at Sebring International Raceway.

Friday, Palou will drive INDY NXT by Firestone machinery for the first time, participating in the Chris Griffis Memorial Test on the 2.439-mile, 14-turn Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course. He is filling in for Chip Ganassi Racing’s full-time INDY NXT driver Carson Etter, who underwent offseason shoulder surgery.

Saturday’s game adds another dimension to Palou’s growing connection with IU. FOX Sports, which became the exclusive television provider of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES ahead of the 2025 season, will broadcast the Ohio State-Indiana matchup.

Palou, the 2025 Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge winner, enters Saturday’s game following a championship season in which he captured his fifth NTT INDYCAR SERIES title. His fourth consecutive championship in 2026 tied him with Sébastien Bourdais, who won four straight titles from 2004-07. No driver has won five consecutive championships. Only A.J. Foyt, with seven titles, and Scott Dixon, with six, have won more career championships than Palou.

title: 2 DAYS AGO •Featured Inside Line: Next First-Time Series Champion?
excerpt:
Today’s question: Who will be the next first-time NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion?

Curt Cavin: Pato O’Ward and Kyle Kirkwood are the past two series runners-up, but I believe Kirkwood (photo, top) is the more likely of the two to climb a higher step, especially as you review his progression since joining the NTT INDYCAR SERIES in 2022. He finished 24th (with AJ Foyt Racing) and then 11th, seventh, fourth and second in four seasons with Andretti Global. I don’t think Kirkwood wins next year’s championship, and he might have to wait a couple of years for Alex Palou to get bored, but I think he will soon earn his way into the champion’s room as his team’s first such winner since Ryan Hunter-Reay in 2012. (By the way, there will soon be significant chatter about Kirkwood being the series’ next big free agent, but I think he remains loyal to Andretti Global and drives the No. 27 Honda for years to come.)

Eric Smith: I believe Scott McLaughlin will be the next first-time champion. If anyone is going to knock Alex Palou off his perch, I don’t see it being a teammate. Scott Dixon couldn’t do it over the past four years, and now he’s moving to Arrow McLaren. If Palou is topped, I sense a down year for the entire Chip Ganassi Racing organization. So why not look to Team Penske, a team with 17 series titles, just one behind Ganassi’s 18? McLaughlin (photo, above) closed out 2026 in strong fashion, posting three consecutive top-five finishes, including a season-finale victory at Laguna Seca. He also knows what it takes to win a championship, having claimed three Australian V8 Supercars titles. McLaughlin is a versatile driver who excels across all disciplines, and his time is coming. I believe he’ll win an INDYCAR SERIES championship within the next two to three years.

Arni Sribhen: The last 14 NTT INDYCAR SERIES champions have raced for either Chip Ganassi Racing or Team Penske, so the odds are high that the next first-time champion is already racing for one of those two teams. In fact, I think David Malukas has the best shot at winning an Astor Challenge Cup among the drivers who haven’t already won one. The evidence is there. Malukas (photo, above) had a breakout first season with Team Penske, though he didn’t reach victory lane. His four runner-up finishes show he’s knocking on the door of that first win, and when that happens, the wins may come in bunches. It’s reminiscent of Simon Pagenaud’s first few seasons with Penske. He was winless in his first season, then won the series championship the next season and was a contender for the next few seasons. I think Malukas may be on that same Penske path.

Paul Kelly: Christian Lundgaard. The Dane (photo, above) earned his first victory in 2023 from the pole on the streets of Toronto, with Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing. Then he added two road-course wins in 2026, at the Sonsio Grand Prix and Road America, with Arrow McLaren. The only missing link to becoming a champion is oval performance, and I think Lundgaard’s shortcomings on circle tracks are dwindling, as evidenced by his third- and sixth-place finishes in August at Milwaukee, the last oval event of the season. That acumen only will increase in Lundgaard’s move to Chip Ganassi Racing, where he will learn the fine art of oval racing from strategist Mike Hull and advisor Dario Franchitti, who also took awhile to figure out circle tracks before flourishing on them. And don’t forget that five-time series champion Alex Palou didn’t earn his first oval win until the 2025 Indianapolis 500, in his sixth season in the series. Finally, Arrow McLaren dumped Lundgaard for what it saw as his weakness on ovals. That stings. So, that rebuke will provide him with any extra motivation he needs. Beating Palou won’t be easy in ANY year, but Lundgaard is best positioned to do it.

title: 2 DAYS AGO •Track News Alex Palou To Help Ganassi Hone INDY NXT Setups at Griffis Test
excerpt:
Track News

Alex Palou has driven plenty of cars around Indianapolis Motor Speedway. This week, he’ll add another to the list.

Five-time and reigning NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion Palou (photo, top) will drive the No. 11 Chip Ganassi Racing entry in the annual Chris Griffis Memorial Test on Friday, Oct. 16, on the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course. Palou is filling in for CGR full-time INDY NXT driver Carson Etter, who is recovering from offseason shoulder surgery.

SEE: Griffis Test Entry List

The test honors Chris Griffis, the team manager for Schmidt Peterson Motorsports who died suddenly in September 2011. Friday’s session allows teams an opportunity to evaluate drivers and experiment with setups to begin preparations for the following season.

Palou is among 22 drivers scheduled to participate in the test, which runs from 9:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m. ET. The Turn 2 spectator mounds will be open to fans.

Palou’s participation puts him in a rare position. He’s the four-time defending NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion stepping into the sport’s top developmental series after establishing himself at its highest level. Palou has never driven INDY NXT machinery. He joined the INDYCAR SERIES in 2020 with Dale Coyne Racing after building his career in European and Japanese series.

An INDY NXT car produces approximately 200-300 less horsepower and less downforce than an INDYCAR SERIES machine, along with different braking characteristics.

“It’ll be tough,” Palou said. “It’s very tough always to go from a car that has more downforce and carbon brakes and stuff to some car that is a bit smaller, less downforce, less power, and it doesn’t have as much performance. I’m excited to help the team see how that car feels.”

Palou believes familiarity with the 14-turn, 2.439-mile circuit helps the learning curve while testing the team's No. 11 INDY NXT car (photo, above). He’s a three-time Sonsio Grand Prix winner, each coming in the past four years.

“I’m excited to see what that car is capable of and helping the team as much as I can,” Palou said. “Its (the car) is probably like the current F3, which I drove almost eight to 10 years ago.

“So, yeah, it’ll take me a little bit to get used to. I know I won’t be at 100%. But I don’t think we don’t need to. The good thing is we’re not racing. We’re just testing. We’re just trying to learn as much as we can.”

Palou has been behind the wheel of many race cars lately. He drove an Acura prototype in the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship race Oct. 3 at Petit Le Mans for Meyer Shank Racing. Palou then practiced and qualified the No. 80 Lone Star Racing Mercedes-AMG in last weekend’s Intercontinental GT Challenge Indianapolis 8 Hour on this same track, but he never turned a racing lap due to an early accident by one of his teammates. On Monday, he tested the IR-28, the new INDYCAR SERIES chassis scheduled to debut in 2028, at Sebring International Raceway.

He’s aware this test represents an opportunity for Chip Ganassi Racing to pursue a milestone that has eluded one of motorsports’ most successful organizations. CGR has amassed 25 championships across racing disciplines, including a record 18th INDYCAR SERIES title in 2026. The team has earned more than 275 victories in motorsports, including six Indianapolis 500 wins, eight Rolex 24 At Daytona victories and six wins apiece in the 12 Hours of Sebring and 24 Hours of Le Mans. But an INDY NXT race victory remains missing from its résumé.

Ganassi aims to change that by bringing Palou in for the day as the team works to find speed and strengthen its program.

The team will also field the No. 10 entry for Alessandro de Tullio, who competed as a rookie with AJ Foyt Racing this past season. De Tullio finished sixth in the championship standings with two victories. His eight pole positions fell one short of Pato O’Ward’s single-season series record set in 2018. Alexander Koreiba and Frankie Mossman join the duo for Friday’s test with CGR.

title: Alexander Rossi Hustles IR-28 Through More Development at Sebring
excerpt:
The development of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES’ next-generation IR-28 car moved this week to the bumps and bruises of Sebring International Raceway from earlier testing on the silky-smooth surface of Indianapolis Motor Speedway.

Alexander Rossi, who drives full time for Chevrolet-powered ECR, took over testing duties Tuesday at the historic Florida circuit. The 2016 Indianapolis 500 winner continued the evaluation of the car that will debut at the start of the 2028 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season.

The Sebring test marks the first opportunity to evaluate the IR-28 away from Indianapolis, following initial sessions on the 2.439-mile, 14-turn road course and 2.5-mile oval in August and September. Five-time and reigning series champion Alex Palou completed 43 laps Monday on Sebring’s outer loop, putting the new car through its paces on a circuit renowned for its punishing surface and demanding mix of asphalt and concrete. Rossi turned 134 laps Tuesday.

Palou, a Honda-powered driver for Chip Ganassi Racing, and Rossi also were chosen to handle testing duties at both IMS configurations.

The two-day Sebring test session represents another important step in the series’ extensive development program, with the IR-28 facing the kind of conditions designed to expose weaknesses long before the car reaches competition.

“It’s a new car for me at Sebring,” Rossi said. “Coming back here and being part of the next generation of INDYCAR’s future is a huge honor. It’s an exciting time in this sport. This car, in so many ways, is a pretty big upgrade from what we have.”

Sebring is a regular testing destination for INDYCAR SERIES teams, in large part because of its unforgiving character. Its bumps, uneven surfaces and relentless demands on vehicle components make it an ideal proving ground for a car expected to compete on road courses, ovals and temporary street circuits. With street circuits accounting for one-third of the 2026 schedule, durability and driver confidence over challenging surfaces remain important considerations in the IR-28’s development.

“What’s good about this place is it’s the poorest-quality surface that you can have in a permanent road course,” Rossi said. “It mimics a street course kind of. Because it’s a permanent road course, it gets used a lot, so it’s a higher grip level than a street course. In terms of bumps, pavement changes, difficult changes in the asphalt, that’s why everyone comes and tests here. It’s somewhat of a preview that you’re going to get in street courses.”

Rossi’s test plan Tuesday focused on evaluating the car’s fundamental systems and performance, building on work completed during earlier sessions at Indianapolis. He worked alongside Dallara and INDYCAR officials.

The testing emphasis has evolved as development has progressed. Initial tests focused on confirming that the car’s systems functioned as expected. At Sebring, the priority was understanding how the package performs over an extended test and identifying issues that might emerge through more extensive running, especially on rough, bumpy surfaces.

“I don’t know that anyone is looking for anything (particular),” Rossi said. “The messaging we get is run the car as if it’s your race car. From there, we’ll see what issues, problems, surprises come out of that. I think all the test list items were really accomplished in the first two tests. Just making sure things worked as you would expect.

“This test is more of a practical application of: ‘Does it perform over a two-day test as the current car does? Does it do what it is expected to and kind of what little things could come out of that we need to address before the series produces a bunch of these?’”

Driver feedback remains central to that process, particularly when it comes to comfort and cockpit cooling. The IR-28 incorporates a more integrated cooling approach, with strategically positioned ducts designed into the initial bodywork rather than added to the existing carbon-fiber structure. Palou reported a significant improvement in cooling during Monday’s running, highlighting progress since the initial Indianapolis tests.

Rossi also experienced the benefits of those improvements at Sebring.

“First of all, visually, it’s an incredible race car to look at,” Rossi said. “It generates more grip in high-speed corners. It’s a very nice car to drive. It’s well-built and incredibly well-engineered. Cooling-wise, we made a pretty big step in this test, in particular. It’s night-and-day different in terms of comfort and drivability in the cockpit.”

Although the car’s competition debut remains more than a year away, the development schedule allows time to address concerns and validate improvements across different types of circuits before the 2028 season begins. Every lap adds another piece to that process, helping ensure the IR-28 can withstand the demands of a race weekend while delivering the performance drivers and fans expect.

“There are more things that are scheduled to come as time comes that will allow this car to race and perform even better, that will only put on a better show for the fans, which is the No. 1 priority for all of us,” Rossi said.

title: Shake It Up: Alex Palou Puts IR-28 Through Pounding Paces at Sebring
excerpt:
INDYCAR Technologies

The initial tests of the new NTT INDYCAR SERIES IR-28 chassis took place in August and September on the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course and oval, two circuits known for their billiard-table smooth asphalt.

Now, for the rough stuff.

Five-time and reigning NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion Alex Palou of Honda-powered Chip Ganassi Racing turned 43 laps Monday on the outer loop at Sebring International Raceway in Sebring, Florida, the first test for the car outside of IMS. 2016 Indianapolis 500 winner Alexander Rossi of Chevrolet-powered ECR will take over testing duties Tuesday at the historic Florida circuit.

Sebring is a popular testing site for NTT INDYCAR SERIES teams due to its bumpy nature and mix of asphalt and concrete surfaces, which simulate well the temporary street circuits that formed a third of the series schedule in 2026. It’s a punishing, unforgiving track that stresses the durability and strength of components perhaps better than any other testing ground for the series.

“We’re trying to test it as tough as we can,” Palou said. “It’s a bumpy course. Before we produce all the new cars, we want to make sure it passes this stress test and that it’s good to go for racing.

“We’re trying to get miles and miles, see what breaks so we can fix it.”

Palou and Rossi are the only series drivers so far to test the car, which will be introduced at the start of the 2028 season. As in the road course and oval tests at IMS, the two drivers and Dallara and INDYCAR officials will continue to perform a long checklist of basic system and performance checks on the car.

But Palou noticed Monday his feedback on driver comfort and car braking from the initial tests at IMS was adopted and made significant improvements, especially in driver cooling. The revolutionary aeroscreen was added to the current car in 2020, with ducts fit into the existing carbon fiber body to aid cooling. The new car has more ducts that are more strategically placed from initial design instead of an add-on like the ducting on the current car.

“Yeah, it’s been so much better, the cooling, since we started a couple months ago,” Palou said. “Huge step, and that’s something we’ve been asking for a long time on our current car.

“We have a very big one (duct) right in front of us (on the IR-28) that makes the air go from down to up and makes the airflow so much better. It’s been huge.”

Palou completed a historic moment for the IR-28 during testing today when he passed a current car driven by Kyle Kirkwood of Andretti Global, who was testing Firestone Firehawk tires at the circuit along with Scott McLaughlin of Team Penske. It was the first on-track pass for the new car.

“It wasn’t planned,” Palou said. “We went out, and I saw Kirkwood was doing the tire test. We spoke during lunch that at some point this afternoon we would go together. We wanted to see how this car does in traffic. It was cool. We were playing a little bit.”

Another advantage to Sebring being a regular test spot for NTT INDYCAR SERIES teams is there’s a plethora of data with the current car that can be compared with the IR-28. All systems continue to be go with the new car.

“I’m very excited,” Palou said. “I like the looks of it. It seems safer. It looks like it’s going to be much better racing because we’re going to be able to follow much closer on road, street and ovals.

“I’m just excited to go racing. I wish it was already ’27. Having said that, it gives us so much time to work on the car, to make sure it’s good. If there’s something that doesn’t really work on ovals or whatever, we can go test it before we actually race it.”

title: A Look at Numbers That Defined 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES Season
excerpt:
Numbers can help tell a story, and in the case of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES they serve as a reflection of the success experienced in the 2026 season.

From competitive on-track action to increased television viewership, the series had one of its best seasons on record.

Here are five numbers that had a significant impact on that success.

10

Begin with what occurred on the track. It was as thrilling as it was competitive, and every team had a shining moment.

All 10 full-time teams led laps, and each made at least one appearance in a Firestone Fast Six qualifying round staged on road and street races. Nine teams earned a podium finish.

Eight drivers won races, the most since 2022. Eight also celebrated NTT P1 Awards as top qualifiers for races.

Sixteen drivers earned a top-three finish, tied for the highest total since 2015.

The 25 full-time starters represented 14 nations.

.0233

That was Felix Rosenqvist’s record-setting margin of victory in the 110th Running of the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge. The separation between Rosenqvist and Team Penske’s David Malukas (photo, above) broke the 1992 mark of .043 of a second (Al Unser Jr. holding back Scott Goodyear).

This “500” featured a sellout for the second consecutive year, and it featured a race-record 70 lead changes, the third-highest total in INDYCAR SERIES history.

Fourteen of the 33 drivers led the race, a total that ranks third all-time. Rosenqvist led 25 laps. Only Palou (59), Scott Dixon (32) and Malukas (30) led more laps.

A record total purse of $30,906,400 was distributed.

5

That’s how many poles Chip Ganassi Racing’s Alex Palou won in a stretch of races during a seven-week stretch between the Sonsio Grand Prix on the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course and the XPEL Grand Prix at Road America, and it included the NTT P1 Award for being the fastest qualifier for the “500.”

Now, the five poles didn’t earn Palou (photo, above) an award, but it was the run that effectively put his championship challengers on severe notice. In that stretch, Palou gained 43 points on second place, the fuel he needed to win a fourth consecutive series title and fifth overall. Palou ended the year with eight poles and six race wins, leading both categories. At one point he led the standings by 133 points en route to an 86-point final margin.

At 29, Palou became the sport’s youngest five-time series champion.

18

Few could have predicted Team Penske’s total number of INDYCAR SERIES championships – 17 – would ever be broken, but it was this year.

Palou delivered Chip Ganassi Racing its record-setting 18th series title (photo, above), and remarkably all have come since 1996 when Jimmy Vasser scored the organization’s first. Team Penske has won eight in that span.

Palou now has five championships – all with CGR. He stands one behind Dixon’s career total, and Dixon also earned them all as a Ganassi driver.

Dario Franchitti won three season titles with CGR, Alex Zanardi two. Vasser and Juan Pablo Montoya added one championship each to Ganassi’s total.

1.68 million

The NTT INDYCAR SERIES reached its largest television audience in nearly two decades, averaging 1.68 million viewers on FOX (photo, above) across the 18 races.

Viewership increased more than 23 percent over the 2025 season and more than 57 percent against 2024. The two years formed one of the most impressive growth curves in sports.

Nine races averaged at least 1 million viewers, the most since the 2008 season. The Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C. averaged 3.28 million viewers, the most for a series race other than the “500” since 1995.

The XPEL Grand Prix at Road America averaged 1.8 million viewers, which at the time was the highest non-Indy 500 race since 2011.

All 18 races, plus four additional events, aired live on network television.

title: INDYCAR Notebook: IR-28 Hits Road for Sebring Test Next Week
excerpt:
INDYCAR Technologies

Testing of the new IR-28 chassis that will be introduced into the NTT INDYCAR SERIES at the start of the 2028 season will continue next week, with laps turned outside of Indianapolis Motor Speedway for the first time.

Five-time and reigning NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion Alex Palou of Chip Ganassi Racing (photo, top) and 2016 Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge winner Alexander Rossi of ECR will continue to serve as drivers of the new car in testing Monday, Oct. 12 and Tuesday, Oct. 13 at Sebring International Raceway. Palou will test Monday, with Rossi taking over Tuesday.

The historic Florida circuit resembles conditions of INDYCAR SERIES temporary street circuits, with a variety of surfaces, including asphalt and concrete, and many bumps.

The test comes after three days of laps by Rossi and Palou in early August on the IMS road course for the car’s on-track debut, followed by the car’s oval debut in testing in early September at IMS.

Also turning laps those two days will be Kyle Kirkwood of Andretti Global and Scott McLaughlin of Team Penske, testing tires for Firestone in current NTT INDYCAR SERIES machinery.

White House Congratulates CGR for Title

Team owner Chip Ganassi received a letter from President Donald J. Trump congratulating him and his Chip Ganassi Racing team for Alex Palou’s fifth NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship this season, the record-setting 18th INDYCAR SERIES title for the organization.

“Chip Ganassi Racing continues to be at the forefront of the racing world,” Trump wrote. “Your team is composed of elite competitors who consistently demonstrate grit, hard work, and dedication.”

Trump, his wife, Melania, and other Cabinet and government officials were honored guests during the Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C. on Aug. 23 on the streets of the nation’s capital.

title: Team Penske To Continue Long Partnership With Chevrolet
excerpt:
Team Penske and Chevrolet announced Oct. 8 a multiyear extension of their partnership that will keep the most successful team in NTT INDYCAR SERIES history with the manufacturer that has powered much of that success.

That heritage of winning includes nine victories in the Indianapolis 500 with drivers Rick Mears, Emerson Fittipaldi, Helio Castroneves, Juan Pablo Montoya, Will Power, Simon Pagenaud and Josef Newgarden.

“Chevrolet has been a terrific partner for our NTT INDYCAR SERIES team, both on and off the track,” Roger Penske said. “While winning on the track is certainly important, Team Penske’s partnership with Chevrolet extends far beyond that. We are excited that this extension will take us well into the future as we work to build on the success we have enjoyed together in the INDYCAR SERIES.”

The 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season saw Team Penske and Chevrolet open the year with the pole position on the streets of St. Petersburg while capping the campaign with a win at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca. For the season, Team Penske added to the Chevrolet victory ledger with wins at Phoenix Raceway, World Wide Technology Raceway and Laguna Seca, respectively, along with earning three pole positions in 2026.

Since officially joining forces for the 1986 INDYCAR SERIES season with a manufacturer-backed relationship, Team Penske and Chevrolet have visited Victory Lane 125 times and have captured 157 pole positions, including Scott McLaughlin’s NTT P1 Award in September at Laguna Seca that represented Chevrolet’s 250th INDYCAR SERIES pole position.

Team Penske first began competing in INDYCAR with legendary driver Mark Donohue driving a Chevrolet-powered Eagle in the USAC-sanctioned race June 15, 1968, at Canadian Tire Motorsports Park.

“For decades, Team Penske and Chevrolet have had one of the strongest competitive relationships in all of motorsport, built on a foundation of trust, a shared commitment to technical excellence, and a relentless focus on winning,” General Motors President Mark Reuss said. “The results of our partnership speak for themselves, but we’re also driven by what comes next. This extension ensures our teams remain aligned and steadfast in our pursuit of more poles, more wins and more Indy 500 victories together.”

This was the third extension agreement between Chevrolet and an INDYCAR SERIES team announced this week, with Penske’s pact joining those signed with Arrow McLaren and ECR.

The 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season starts Sunday, March 7 on the streets of St. Petersburg, Florida.

title: Inside Line: Top Ganassi Championship Season?
excerpt:
Today’s question: Chip Ganassi Racing won its record-setting 18th NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship this year. What’s one of those championship seasons you’d like to highlight?

Curt Cavin: The 1996 season was embroiled in the politics of a divided sport, so many of the accomplishments of the drivers and their teams didn’t get the credit they deserved. Among those was Jimmy Vasser, who became Chip Ganassi Racing’s first season championship in ‘96. That year, Jimmy (photo, above, center) won three of Champ Car’s first four races and then won the highly anticipated U.S. 500, the Memorial Day weekend race at Michigan International Speedway that countered the Indy Racing League’s Indianapolis 500. Jimmy finished the season 22 points ahead of Michael Andretti and Alex Zanardi while besting a field that included eight drivers who earned series championships in their careers. Because of the split, Jimmy didn’t participate at Indy for four of his best years in the sport, so his talent isn’t as regarded as it should have been. Jimmy had two other top-three series finishes (third in ’97, second in ’98), and he won eight poles and 10 races amid that highly competitive late-1990s.

Eric Smith: It’s 2009 for me. Dario Franchitti rejoined the INDYCAR SERIES following a disappointing year in NASCAR. He won the 2007 INDYCAR SERIES title with Andretti Autosport, left to join CGR in NASCAR, then returned to open-wheel racing in 2009 and won a narrow championship by 11 points over teammate Scott Dixon. Franchitti won the season finale while Dixon tried to stretch his fuel strategy but had to pit with eight laps to go at Homestead. He finished third in the race but second in the championship, one of three times the team finished 1-2 occurred joining 1998 and 2023. Franchitti (photo, top, right) and Dixon (photo, top, left) combined to win 10 of the 17 races that year, tying 1998 for the most wins by a team in a single season. Franchitti had 15 top-10 finishes, while Dixon had 14.

Arni Sribhen: Dario Franchitti thought he was done with INDYCAR SERIES racing after winning both the Indianapolis 500 and NTT INDYCAR SERIES title in 2007. But after a brief and aborted foray into NASCAR with Chip Ganassi Racing in 2008, Ganassi put Franchitti back in an INDYCAR SERIES car for 2009. And what a comeback season it was. Franchitti won five races, including a masterclass in fuel saving at Homestead, to steal the title from reigning champion Scott Dixon and Team Penske’s Ryan Briscoe. It was the first of three straight title wins for Franchitti and paired with two Indy 500 wins over the next four seasons, lifted him into the status of one of this generation’s greats.

Paul Kelly: It’s absolutely 2009 for me, too, for so many reasons – some also listed above. Dario Franchitti and Scott Dixon finished 1-2 in the standings and won 10 of 17 races. This wasn’t the first time Chip Ganassi Racing drivers finished 1-2 in the standings – Alex Zanardi and Jimmy Vasser first achieved the feat in 1998 for the team. And it wasn’t the last, as Alex Palou and Dixon were 1-2 in 2023. But I elevate 2009 over those other two seasons for two reasons. One, Franchitti and Dixon were the team’s only drivers in 2009, yet they still finished 1-2. Team Penske drivers have finished 1-2 in the standings five times since 2014, an incredible achievement. But those were three- or four-driver teams, so Penske could have a driver or two with a down year and still have a shot at finishing 1-2. Two, Franchitti and Dixon were so competitive with each other in 2009. Franchitti finished just 11 points ahead of his teammate. In 1998, Zanardi was 116 points ahead of Vasser, and Palou beat Dixon by 78 in 2023. The 2009 race featured true competition between two all-time greats of the sport. It was fantastic.

title: ECR, Chevrolet Agree to Multiyear Partnership Extension
excerpt:
ECR and Chevrolet announced Oct. 7 a multiyear extension of their longstanding partnership.

Indianapolis-based ECR is one of only two teams to have been powered by Chevrolet since the introduction of the 2.2-liter twin-turbo V6. During the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season, ECR will reach its 500th race start, continuing a relationship with Chevrolet that dates back to the team’s inception in 2012.

The extension comes as the NTT INDYCAR SERIES prepares to introduce a new chassis and engine formula in 2028. Alexander Rossi, driver of ECR’s No. 20 Java House Chevrolet, is one of two drivers to have participated in the first tests of the series’ new chassis. As development progresses, ECR will have the opportunity to be involved in testing Chevrolet’s new powerplant.

“Chevrolet has been with ECR since the beginning of our team, and they have been an important part of our team’s growth over our first 15 seasons,” ECR co-owner and CEO Ed Carpenter said. “We’ve had a lot of success with Chevy over the years, and we’re proud to be one of only two teams to have partnered with Chevrolet since its return to INDYCAR. Maintaining that continuity is very important to us as we not only approach our 500th race start but also enter the next era of INDYCAR competition.

“We’re very proud of our history with Chevrolet and are looking forward to adding to it.”

ECR and Chevrolet have won nine races and six NTT P1 Awards together, including three poles by Carpenter for the Indianapolis 500.

“ECR has been an important part of Chevrolet’s INDYCAR program, and this extension reflects the strength of the technical relationship we’ve built together,” said Eric Warren, General Motors vice president of global motorsports competition. “As the series moves toward its next-generation car and powertrain, close collaboration between our engineers will be critical. We share a clear objective with ECR: to keep raising the performance of the Chevrolet package and compete for wins, championships and Indianapolis 500 victories.”

The 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season begins Sunday, March 7 on the streets of St. Petersburg, Florida.

title: Arrow McLaren Staying With Chevrolet Power for Multiple Seasons
excerpt:
Arrow McLaren announced Oct. 6 a multiyear extension with Chevrolet as its engine manufacturer, reaffirming the organizations’ longstanding technical partnership as the NTT INDYCAR SERIES prepares for its next era of innovation.

The extension comes at a pivotal moment for both Arrow McLaren and Chevrolet as the series completes early testing phases for the new Dallara IR-28 chassis set to debut in 2028 competition. The next generation platform will introduce improved aerodynamic architecture, an upgraded power-to-weight ratio, new wing packages designed for better racing and overall improved safety systems — all areas where early manufacturer involvement is essential.

"Our extension with Chevrolet is key to our overall goal of winning both the INDYCAR championship and the Indy 500,” McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown said. “Over the past seven seasons, the team and Chevy have been working closely together through various developments, and the work now ahead of us with the 2028 chassis will be critical in determining our competitiveness. Mark Reuss, Eric Warren, Jim Campbell and everyone across the Chevy and GM organization are committed to executing at the highest level and share our absolute focus on winning. I’m excited for what’s to come with this strengthened relationship."

Since McLaren Racing entered the series full time in 2020 with Schmidt Peterson Motorsports to become Arrow McLaren SP, the Arrow McLaren and Chevrolet collaboration has achieved 14 Chevy-powered wins, 54 podiums and 13 NTT P1 Awards. Chevy also secured three consecutive Manufacturers’ Championships from 2022-24.

“Arrow McLaren has been an important part of Chevrolet’s INDYCAR program, and this extension reflects the strength of the technical relationship we’ve built together,” said Eric Warren, General Motors vice president of global motorsports competition. “As the series moves toward the next generation of car and powertrain development, close collaboration between our engineers will be critical. We continue to share a clear objective with Arrow McLaren: to keep raising the performance of the Chevrolet package and compete for wins, championships and the Indianapolis 500."

Team veteran Pato O’Ward welcomes six-time series champion Scott Dixon and 2026 Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge winner Felix Rosenqvist to the team’s three-driver lineup starting in 2027.

title: Friendly Rivalry Reaches Top Level for Kyle Kirkwood, David Malukas
excerpt:
Kyle Kirkwood and David Malukas have followed remarkably similar paths to the top of the sport.

They raced each other in Florida karting events as kids, battled for an INDY NXT championship and now compete for two of the most successful teams in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES. Their careers have taken different turns, but the longtime friendly rivals share a common goal: catching Alex Palou.

Palou, who turned 29 on April 1, has won five championships in six NTT INDYCAR SERIES seasons with Chip Ganassi Racing. His four consecutive titles from 2023-26 tie Sébastien Bourdais’ 2004-07 run for the longest championship streak in series history.

Kirkwood, who turns 28 on Oct. 19, is from Jupiter, Florida, and drives for Andretti Global. Malukas, who turned 25 on Sept. 27, is from Chicago and races for Team Penske. Both believe they can be among the drivers capable of challenging Palou’s dominance.

“It’s crazy to see how far we’ve come,” Malukas said. “Now he’s (Kirkwood) with Andretti. I’m at Penske, and that battle still continues. So, it’s cool to see us as a generation make it all the way to the top.”

Their rivalry began long before either reached the NTT INDYCAR SERIES. Kirkwood and Malukas started racing karts in Florida in 2009. They continued competing against each other through the junior ranks before emerging as the two dominant drivers of the 2021 INDY NXT season. Kirkwood won the championship by 13 points over Malukas, with the pair combining to win 17 of the season’s 20 races (photo, above. Credit: Gavin Baker Photography).

Their paths eventually led to the NTT INDYCAR SERIES, where both were part of the 2022 rookie class. Kirkwood drove for AJ Foyt Racing, while Malukas joined Dale Coyne Racing.

Kirkwood moved to Andretti Global for the 2023 season and quickly established himself as a race winner, earning his first series victory in the prestigious Acura Grand Prix of Long Beach, the third event of the season. He added another win later that year on the streets of Nashville.

Malukas’ progression took a more complicated route. After two seasons with Dale Coyne Racing, he was scheduled to join Arrow McLaren in 2024. But an offseason mountain biking accident left him injured and unable to compete. The team released him before he made a start.

Malukas returned to competition with Meyer Shank Racing for the final 10 races of the 2024 season before spending 2025 with Foyt’s team. Then came his biggest opportunity yet. Team Penske signed Malukas for the 2026 season, giving him the chance to drive for one of the most successful organizations in INDYCAR SERIES history.

It also put two drivers who had competed against each other since childhood in positions they once could only have imagined. Kirkwood was established at Andretti Global. Malukas was now wearing Team Penske colors. Their careers had taken different turns, but the friendly rivalry remained.

“We’ve been through it all,” Malukas said of Kirkwood. “We went through different ranks. We went through feeder series. We’ve been racing each other since I was picking my nose, playing with Hot Wheels, go-karting. The Florida Winter Tour -- that’s where the battle all started.”

This isn’t the first time for a connection like this. Tony Kanaan and Helio Castroneves took a similar path from competing as kids in Brazil to junior open-wheel categories in the United States to the INDYCAR SERIES. The same type of friendly rivalry existed through junior categories for Pato O’Ward and Colton Herta, especially in their fierce race for the INDY NXT title in 2018.

Kirkwood sees the same connection. So much so, he ran into Malukas’ father, Henry, before he climbed into his car in the season finale at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca. Kirkwood said he and Malukas’ dad reflected on how far the two drivers had come.

“I said it’s cool if you look back at when we were in karting together,” Kirkwood said. “We were on the same team in karting many years ago. It’s pretty cool to look and be like, ‘Hey, we’re fighting for positions in a championship, pretty high positions in a championship in INDYCAR.’”

Kirkwood finished second in points in the 2026 season while Malukas was fifth, the top Team Penske points finisher. Kirkwood is well aware what makes Malukas such a formidable opponent, one he believes will earn his first series win sooner than later.

“He’s a phenomenal driver,” Kirkwood said. “He definitely does the things that I do poorly extremely well. I’ve learned a lot racing against him over the years.”

That familiarity could become an advantage as both drivers continue their pursuit of Palou. They know each other’s strengths. They have watched each other develop. And they have competed against each other every step of the way. Now, they have the equipment and experience to contend at the front of the championship.

“I’m proud to be part of the era he’s in because he’s an exceptional driver,” Kirkwood said. “I think for many years to come, he’s going to be someone knocking on the door of a championship.”

title: Surprise, Surprise: Biggest 2026 Stunners in NTT INDYCAR SERIES
excerpt:
Sports seasons regularly produce surprises, which is part of what makes them endearing. The NTT INDYCAR SERIES certainly had its share of surprises in 2026.

Of course, Chip Ganassi Racing’s Alex Palou winning a fourth consecutive season championship and fifth in six years wasn’t one of them. And a second consecutive sellout of the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge, which occurred in May, was largely expected given the momentum the event and the sport have built in recent years.

It also wasn’t much of a surprise that television viewership of races took another large gain – a 23 percent year-over-year increase – given the investment and commitment FOX has made in the sport. But there were plenty of things that caught people off guard this year. A look at them somewhat sequentially.

INDYCAR Having a Street Race Where?!

There had only been whispers of a new street race in the nation’s capital, but it seemed like a dream that couldn’t come true. So, the news was a shocker when it was announced Jan. 30.

Along with the “500,” the Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C. on Aug. 23 became a signature moment of the season, the kind of event that almost seemed incomprehensible given the hurdles that needed to be overcome and the city’s magnificent backdrops.

Television ratings were through the roof: 3.28 million people tuned in, making it the most-watched race other than Indy since 1995.

The Washington race (photo, above) was one of three new street races in 2026, and each contributed to the success of the season. With the support of the Dallas Cowboys and the Texas Rangers, the Java House Grand Prix of Arlington will be keeper along with the Ontario Honda Dealers Indy at Markham, a relocation of the Toronto street race.

Andretti Global drivers captured all three events, with Kyle Kirkwood winning in Arlington and Washington and Marcus Ericsson victorious in Markham.

Schumacher (Yes, That Schumacher!) Shines on Ovals

The series’ return to Phoenix Raceway for the first time since 2018 went very well, and one of the standouts made his oval-track debut.

Mick Schumacher is best known for being the only son of seven-time Formula One champion Michael Schumacher, who often made it clear he didn’t want any part of INDYCAR’s high-speed oval thrillers. But Mick (photo, above) adapted just fine, so much so that his best performances in the first year in this series were on oval tracks.

Driving Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing’s No. 47 Honda, Schumacher was quick straight away at Phoenix, qualifying in the fourth position. In the race, he remained on the lead lap until his crew struggled with a tire change on the pit stop at Lap 71. That bobble dropped Schumacher to the 21st position; he finished the race in 18th place.

That was a preview of oval success to come for the Swiss-born German driver. Schumacher completed all 200 laps in the “500,” finishing a respectable 18th to earn Rookie of the Year honors. He backed up that performance by finishing 16th in the Bommarito Automotive Group 500 at World Wide Technology Raceway, was eighth in the Borchetta Bourbon Music City Grand Prix at Nashville Superspeedway and earned the 13th- and 12th-place finishes in the Snap-on INDYCAR Weekend, a doubleheader at the tricky Milwaukee Mile.

Schumacher finished second to Dale Coyne Racing’s Dennis Hauger for the series’ Rookie of the Year Award. AJ Foyt Racing’s Caio Collet finished third.

Rosenqvist Wins Indy in a Thriller

Felix Rosenqvist certainly had been competitive in past oval races at Indianapolis Motor Speedway, finishing fourth in 2022 and 2025. But he’d never had a final lap like he delivered in this year’s race – in fact, no one had.

Rosenqvist, who had started fourth and led 24 laps, began Lap 200 in the third position. He got a terrific run coming to the white flag and drew alongside Meyer Shank Racing w/ Curb Agajanian teammate Marcus Armstrong as they crossed the historic Yard of Bricks.

Winning Indy is never easy, and this one certainly wasn’t for the Swede. He spent most of the lap driving on the outside of Armstrong before finally clearing him in the middle of Turn 4. From there it seemed like Rosenqvist’s car was shot out of a cannon as he quickly closed on race leader David Malukas of Team Penske, sweeping past him just ahead of the checkered flag. The separation was a scant .0233 of a second (photo, above), the closest 1-2 finish in the history of “The Greatest Spectacle in Racing.” The previous record was .043 of a second in 1992.

The breathtaking race featured an event-record 70 lead changes, breaking the previous mark of 68 set in 2013. With his second career NTT INDYCAR SERIES victory, Rosenqvist became the third Swedish driver to win Indy, joining Kenny Brack (1999) and Ericsson (2022). Meyer Shank Racing won the “500” for a second time, the other being Helio Castroneves’ record-tying fourth victory in 2021.

Dixon’s Switch Biggest of Silly Season

After 25 seasons and six NTT INDYCAR SERIES championships, Scott Dixon made the startling switch of employers, leaving Chip Ganassi Racing for Arrow McLaren.

Dixon (photo, top) had won 58 races and six series championships with Chip Ganassi’s organization, the partnership becoming an all-time standard in the sport. Dixon joined the team in 2002 and ended his time there after 414 starts, including a series-record 374 consecutively.

Joining Dixon on the move was Rosenqvist, who became the first reigning “500” champion since 2017 winner Takuma Sato to switch teams for the next season. Dixon and Rosenqvist will join Pato O’Ward and Ryan Hunter-Reay for the team’s stellar cast at Indy.

CGR filled Dixon’s seat with Christian Lundgaard, whom Arrow McLaren chose not to re-sign after winning two races and finishing third in the final point standings. MSR elevated Armstrong, who finished fifth at Indy, and added Schumacher for next season.

Schumacher’s former team – Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing – announced it will be a two-car operation in 2027. Dreyer & Reinbold Racing will join the series full-time with Conor Daly as its Honda driver after purchasing a charter from RLL. Several other seats for next year’s lineup are still to be determined.

VeeKay, Juncos Hollinger Racing Earn Top-10 Standing

Rinus VeeKay and Juncos Hollinger Racing took a bite out of many of the sport’s big dogs by finishing 10th in the standings, the highest career finish for both the driver and the team.

VeeKay (photo, above) had finished 12th in two previous seasons – in 2021 and 2023 – while JHR’s prior best was 16th in 2023 with Callum Ilott at the wheel.

This pairing finished third in the second race of the Snap-on INDYCAR Weekend doubleheader at the Milwaukee Mile and added three fourth-place finishes. Somewhat overlooked was another outstanding performance: sixth in the “500,” a best finish for the driver and the team.

title: INDYCAR Drivers Extending Seasons at Petit Le Mans IMSA Finale
excerpt:
Drivers from the NTT INDYCAR SERIES and INDY NXT by Firestone are extending their racing seasons by competing in all four classes of Motul Petit Le Mans, the season-ending IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship race Oct. 1-3 at Road Atlanta.

INDYCAR SERIES champions Scott Dixon and Alex Palou will be teammates – perhaps for the last time after their six seasons together at Chip Ganassi Racing – in the premier Grand Touring Prototype (GTP) class in the 10-hour race Saturday, sharing separate entries for Acura Meyer Shank Racing w/Curb Agajanian.

Six-time series champion Dixon will share the No. 60 Acura ARX-06 with former INDYCAR SERIES drivers Tom Blomqvist and Colin Braun on the 12-turn, 2.54-mile road course in Braselton, Georgia. Dixon is leaving Chip Ganassi Racing at the end of this year after 24 full-time seasons to join Arrow McLaren next season in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES.

Five-time series champion Palou will start two consecutive weekends of sports car racing by sharing the No. 93 Acura ARX-06 (photo, top; courtesy IMSA Photo) with Nick Yelloly and Renger van der Zande. Palou also is driving in the Indianapolis 8 Hour Intercontinental GT Challenge race Oct. 10 on the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course.

Palou and Dixon have a good chance at overall victory Saturday if speed in the opening practice Thursday is any indication. Yelloly was quickest at 1 minute, 11.506 seconds in the No. 93, while Braun was a whisker slower at 1:11.509 in the No. 60.

Not only is this event an end to Dixon and Palou as teammates, but it also marks the end of Acura’s prototype program in IMSA and with MSR.

In another note of interest in the GTP class, former INDYCAR SERIES driver Colton Herta is returning to America to share the No. 40 Cadillac Wayne Taylor Racing Cadillac V-Series.R with Jordan Taylor and Louis Deletraz. Herta had a disappointing first season in 2026 in Formula 2, the final step on the ladder to Formula One.

The GT Daytona PRO (GTD PRO) class features two INDY NXT by Firestone champions among its driver lineups.

2021 INDY NXT champion and 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES runner-up Kyle Kirkwood will return to the No. 14 Vasser Sullivan Racing Lexus RC F GT3 as a teammate to former INDYCAR SERIES and INDY NXT driver Jack Hawksworth and Ben Barnicoat. Kirkwood was quickest in the class in practice Thursday.

Freshly crowned INDY NXT champion Nikita Johnson will race in the No. 59 RLL Team McLaren McLaren 720S EVO GT3 (photo, above) that he also drove in the TireRack.com Battle on the Bricks on Sept. 20 at IMS.

The Le Mans Prototype 2 (LMP2) and GT Daytona (GTD) classes each feature one active INDY NXT by Firestone driver.

Jacob Abel is sharing the No. 18 Era Motorsport LMP2 car, while James Roe is in the driver lineup for the No. 80 Lone Star Racing Mercedes-AMG GT3 in GTD.

Live coverage of the 10-hour race begins from noon-3 p.m. ET Saturday on NBC, followed by 3-10:30 p.m. ET on NBCSN. The entire race also will be streamed on Peacock.
